questions.q: What does the standby-side `primary_conninfo` setting do?
options: Provides the connection string (host, port, credentials) the standby uses to stream from the primary
Sets the maximum number of WAL sender processes on the primary
Enables read-only queries on the standby
Names the replication slot the primary should use
questions.explain: primary_conninfo is the standby-side GUC that tells it how to reach and authenticate to the primary for streaming.

questions.q: What role does the standby.signal file play?
options: Its presence in the data directory tells PostgreSQL on startup that this instance is a standby, not a primary
It stores the standby's replication lag in seconds
It is the log file for streaming replication errors
It contains the primary's WAL sender configuration
questions.explain: PostgreSQL checks for the existence of standby.signal (its content doesn't matter) to determine standby mode at startup.

questions.q: What problem does a replication slot solve?
options: It prevents the primary from removing WAL that a lagging or disconnected standby still needs to catch up
It compresses WAL records before they're streamed
It automatically promotes a standby to primary on failover
It encrypts the replication connection
questions.explain: A slot tracks how much WAL its standby has confirmed receiving and tells the primary not to remove WAL past that point.

questions.q: What is the risk of a replication slot for a standby that has been permanently decommissioned but never dropped?
options: WAL will pile up indefinitely on the primary's disk because the slot keeps telling it not to remove that WAL
The primary will refuse to start until the slot is dropped
It has no downside — unused slots are automatically cleaned up
It will silently corrupt data on the primary
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that an unused slot needs to be dropped, since it will otherwise cause unbounded WAL retention.

questions.q: What does enabling hot standby allow?
options: The standby can serve read-only client queries while it continues replaying streamed WAL in the background
The standby can accept write transactions in addition to the primary
The standby automatically becomes the new primary if the original primary fails
The standby stops needing a replication slot
questions.explain: Hot standby lets a replica answer SELECT queries concurrently with ongoing WAL replay, enabling read-scaling patterns.
